question: What does Article 14 guarantee?
expected_key_facts: The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law
The State shall not deny to any person the equal protection of the laws
This protection applies within the territory of India

question: What freedoms are protected by Article 19?
expected_key_facts: All citizens have the right to freedom of speech and expression
All citizens have the right to assemble peaceably and without arms
All citizens have the right to form associations or unions
All citizens have the right to move freely throughout the territory of India

question: What is the right to life and personal liberty under Article 21?
expected_key_facts: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty
Deprivation is only allowed according to procedure established by law

question: What remedies are available under Article 32?
expected_key_facts: Article 32 guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court to enforce fundamental rights
The Supreme Court has the power to issue directions, orders, or writs for enforcing fundamental rights

question: What does Article 72 say about the President's pardoning power?
expected_key_facts: The President has the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment
The President can suspend, remit, or commute the sentence of a person convicted of an offence

question: Can the state deprive someone of life or personal liberty without following a lawful procedure?
expected_key_facts: No, the state cannot deprive a person of life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law
Article 21 protects life and personal liberty

question: Does the Constitution promise equal treatment before the law?
expected_key_facts: Yes, Article 14 guarantees equality before the law
Article 14 also guarantees equal protection of the laws

question: Which constitutional remedy lets a person approach the Supreme Court to enforce fundamental rights?
expected_key_facts: Article 32 lets a person move the Supreme Court directly to enforce fundamental rights
The Supreme Court can issue writs to enforce fundamental rights

question: What freedom protects a person's ability to speak and express opinions?
expected_key_facts: Article 19(1)(a) protects freedom of speech and expression
This is one of the freedoms guaranteed to all citizens under Article 19

question: What did the Supreme Court hold about Article 21 in Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India?
expected_key_facts: The Court held that the procedure depriving someone of life or personal liberty must be fair, just, and reasonable
Articles 14, 19, and 21 must be read together, not as isolated provisions
The case overturned the narrower reading of Article 21 from A.K. Gopalan (1950)

question: Why did Maneka Gandhi's impounded passport raise a natural justice question?
expected_key_facts: Maneka Gandhi's passport was impounded without being told the reasons
She was not given a hearing or an opportunity to be heard before the passport was impounded
This raised the question of whether the procedure followed was fair under Article 21

question: What did the Court strike down in Shreya Singhal v. Union of India and why?
expected_key_facts: The Court struck down Section 66A of the Information Technology Act
Section 66A was struck down as unconstitutional for violating Article 19(1)(a), freedom of speech and expression
Section 66A's vague and undefined terms had a chilling effect on free speech
